claims.text: A controlled increase in lattice distortion in a single-phase high-entropy alloy will increase yield strength.
A controlled increase in lattice distortion in a single-phase high-entropy alloy will increase hardness.
Minor dopant addition can be used to increase lattice distortion while phase stability and other relevant variables remain constant.
A targeted thermal treatment can increase lattice distortion while phase stability and other relevant variables remain constant.
Localized lattice distortion alters the energy landscape encountered by moving dislocations.
Lattice distortion creates barriers that impede dislocation glide.
Dislocations in HEAs can move through local segment depinning from lattice heterogeneities.
Greater resistance to dislocation glide produces higher yield or flow strength.
Greater resistance to dislocation glide produces higher hardness.
Samples with deliberately increased lattice distortion will show statistically significant increases in both hardness and yield strength relative to the baseline.
Increased lattice distortion will produce enhanced dislocation pinning and higher dislocation density.
TEM and XRD line broadening can reveal the proposed enhanced dislocation pinning, dislocation density, and lattice distortion.
As-casting or annealing can provide a single-phase HEA baseline with minimal lattice distortion by relieving internal strain.
The proposed relationship should hold only while the alloy remains a single-phase solid solution without phase transformation or diffusion-induced relief of distortion.
The relationship should remain observable up to approximately 1073 K.
Dynamic recovery or recrystallization would limit the proposed strengthening behavior.
The magnitude of strengthening may depend on dopant concentration, dopant identity, thermal treatment, dislocation-core structure, and local chemical ordering.
Thermal activation near the upper temperature boundary may mask the contribution of lattice distortion.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant increase, exemplified as less than 10% improvement in hardness and yield strength, is designated as a falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: A minor dopant addition necessarily changes composition, but the design also requires the doped and baseline samples to have identical overall compositions.
Applying a targeted thermal treatment changes processing history, whereas the comparison is also required to maintain identical processing histories.

Statistical significance and a 10% effect-size threshold are treated as interchangeable even though an effect below 10% can be statistically significant and an effect above 10% can be statistically nonsignificant.
